response.rationale: Most of the cited evidence (cenoz-2003, cenoz-2013, sanz-2000, thomas-1988, lechner-2014) finds that prior-language knowledge and bilingualism are linked to better L3 outcomes, and the transfer-model papers (CEM, LPM, TPM) show cross-linguistic influence in L3 acquisition, but the evidence is mostly reviews, theory and small studies. It includes conditions such as literacy and formal training, and the receptive-multilingualism items cover comprehension rather than proficiency, so the support is moderate and not strong.
